title: "GEN242: Data Analysis in Genome Biology"
subtitle: "Graduate course materials by Thomas Girke — University of California, Riverside"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

This course introduces computational approaches for working with genomics and related data.
It covers core concepts, algorithms, reproducible data analysis workflows,
and associated programming skills. Students gain practical experience in data analysis
programming, visualization, and interpretation of genomics results.

## Course components

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Slides](slides/index.qmd)
Conceptual background for the course topics. The slides introduce key concepts
and methods required for data analysis in genome biology and related fields.
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Tutorials](tutorials/index.qmd)
Practicals that turn lecture concepts into executable analyses. The
tutorials provide example code for data analysis, visualization, and
reproducible reports.
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .g-col-md-4}
### [Assignments](assignments/index.qmd)
Exercises and course projects that apply the learned material to small research
projects. Project topics change each year based on students' interests.
:::

:::
